newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, bounce seen stalling.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, bounce seen stalling.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday, with gold and silver off the session's highs, and the three day recovery from a three week downtrend may be stalling, analysts said.
"We've seen this often in recent weeks, rallies just can't hold up," Merrill Lynch senior commodities strategist, Bill O'Neill said.
"The strength of the dollar, equities and bond market is providing no incentive for precious metals investors and producers are likely to sell into any further bounce," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down 40 cents at $385.30 an ounce, though the contract pushed higher for the third day early to $386.30.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $382.40/382.80, compared to the London afternoon fix Wednesday at $382.40 and the New York close Tuesday at $382.60-383.10.
COMEX December silver ended down 1.3 cents at $4.922, after pushing higher to $4.960 early.

Renewed concerns emerged about the IMF gold sale plan afer U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said the proposed gold sale would eventually go ahead despite current opposition, the International Herald Tribune reported.
But German Finance Minister Theo Waigel again repeated Germany's opposition to the plan Wednesday.
The plan to sell five million of the IMF's 104 million ounce reserve needs 85 percent approval by IMF member countries but Germany, Switzerland and some other countries remain opposed.

NYMEX October platinum ended unchanged at $390.00 an ounce, after trading in a $390.00-391.00 range, while NYMEX December palladium ended up $1.30 an ounce at $120.50, after trading in a $119.75-120.75 range.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
